title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The sheet is the back of an older typescript (page 42), photographed upside down. It has nothing to do with the motivic notes on the facing pages; Grothendieck evidently reused old typescript sheets as scratch paper. The typed text is an expository proof in descent theory, in the style of the late-1950s/early-1960s descent material (FGA 'Technique de descente' / SGA 1 era).

Setting: f : X' → X, with X'' = X' ×_X X' and g : X'' → X. F' is an object (a sheaf, or an object of a fibered category 𝔉) on X' with descent data. The task is to show the descent data are effective.

Step 1. Define G on X as the equalizer G → f_*(F') ⇉ g_*(F''). By adjunction this gives f^*(G) → F', which is compatible with the descent data. It remains to show it is an isomorphism.

Step 2. Suppose a base change h : Y → X commutes with the formation of f_*(F') and g_*(F''). Then h^*(G) = G_Y is the sheaf obtained by the same equalizer construction from F'_Y on Y' = X' ×_X Y. Moreover, the map f_Y^*(G_Y) → F'_Y is the base change of f^*(G) → F'.

Step 3. Take Y = X' and h = f, assuming this base change commutes with f_* and g_*. The projection Y' = X' ×_X X' → Y = X' has a section (the diagonal), so it is a morphism of effective descent for every fibered category. Hence f_Y^*(G_Y) → F'_Y is an isomorphism. That is, f^*(G) → F' becomes an isomorphism after the base change X' ×_X X' → X'.

Step 4. That base change again has a section. Pulling back along the section recovers f^*(G) → F' itself, so it is an isomorphism and the descent is effective.

9.4.2: This proves Theorem 9.4 in case a), using 5.6 (presumably the case where f_* commutes with base change, e.g. flat base change). Case b), f proper, follows likewise from the fact that for f proper, f_* commutes with every base change Y' → Y; this is announced to be proved in a later exposé. 9.4.3 begins case c) by localizing on Y.

This is a standard reduction-to-a-section argument in descent theory.
errors: Typo in the typescript: 'a une section sur Y' = X'' should read 'over Y = X'' (the projection Y' → Y = X' has the diagonal as a section).
Minor imprecision: '(F_Y)'' should be F'_Y; Y' is used both for X' ×_X Y and for X' ×_X X', which is consistent here since Y = X'.

The claim that f_* commutes with every base change for f proper is true for, e.g., étale/constructible torsion sheaves (proper base change), but not for arbitrary sheaves. The context (a fibered category 𝔉, unspecified) determines its validity; it is deferred to 'un exposé ultérieur'.

ideas.what: Construct the descended object as the equalizer G → f_*F' ⇉ g_*F'' and check effectivity after base change
ideas.modern_name: Descent via equalizer / Beck–Chevalley base-change condition
ideas.where_published: FGA 'Technique de descente I' (Sém. Bourbaki 190); SGA 1 Exp. VI and VIII

ideas.what: A morphism admitting a section is of effective descent for any fibered category, and one may reduce to this case by the base change f itself
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms with a section are effective descent morphisms; descent of isomorphisms

ideas.what: Effective descent along proper surjective morphisms, via commutation of f_* with base change (proper base change)
ideas.modern_name: Proper (h-/cdh-type) descent for sheaves; proper base change
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. VIII (descente), XII (changement de base propre)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the reverse of a recycled typescript page with standard descent-theory material (equalizer construction, reduction to a morphism with a section, proper base change), all of it in SGA 1/SGA 4. It is unrelated to the motivic manuscript on the neighbouring pages and contains nothing new.
